We absolutely hear your risk concerns. Two constraints from our side:
- The board requires indemnity for clinical-safety-related downstream losses; they will not accept a pure mutual exclusion in those scenarios.
- Procurement prefers not to stall the deal for legal fights; if you can offer a pragmatic one-way with a reasonable sub-cap and explicit exclusions for punitive/special damages, it may pass.

Would you accept: one-way carveout limited to documented clinical downstream losses, capped at $2M, excluding punitive, and tied to incidents confirmed as the vendor's proximate cause? If so, we can mark this as a commercial ask (not a legal blocker).

Tessa / Laura — quick read: thanks for the summary and the options doc. My initial thoughts:

- We should avoid an open-ended one-way carveout. If we must accept any one-way exposure, tie it to a very tight definition ("Documented Clinical Impact" where customer proves: (i) service outage directly caused measurable patient-impact metrics defined in SOW; (ii) downstream regulatory fines expressly caused by vendor negligence; and (iii) the incident was escalated into our incident response within 48 hours).
- Put the $2M sub-cap under the overall contract cap (i.e., $2M sub-limit that counts against the aggregate cap) and include a requirement for third-party verification of losses over $250k (to deter speculative claims).
- Add mitigations: mandatory post-incident root cause analysis, limited remediation credits, and a 30-day cure window before claims for consequential losses can be asserted.

If legal is comfortable with a narrow defined category + verification + process guards, that may be acceptable commercially. Laura — can you draft two short alternative paragraphs: (1) mutual exclusion with narrow "clinical impact" carveout (customer-only), and (2) mutual exclusion plus a carveout that is reciprocal but lower sub-caps? We will present both to customer.

Karthik

Team — drafted three candidate clauses (text pasted below). I recommend we present Option 2 to BrightHealth as the fastest path; Option 1 is our preferred risk posture but will likely be rejected. Option 3 is an emergency fallback if BD needs the deal signed this week.

Option 1 (Preferred — mutual exclusion w/ narrow clinical exception):
"Except as provided in this Section, neither Party shall be liable for incidental, consequential, special or punitive damages. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either Party may recover documented Clinical Impact Losses arising from a failure of the Services where: (i) the loss is a direct, proximate result of Vendor gross negligence or willful misconduct; (ii) such loss is specifically identified in an applicable SOW; and (iii) Customer provides written notice and allows Vendor 30 days to investigate and cure. Documented Clinical Impact Losses are subject to the aggregate cap in Section X."

Option 2 (Commercial compromise — customer-favored one-way carveout with process/verification):
"Except as provided in this Section, neither Party shall be liable for incidental, consequential, special or punitive damages. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may recover Documented Clinical Impact Losses up to Two Million Dollars (US $2,000,000) provided that: (i) Customer demonstrates by contemporaneous documentation that the loss is the direct and proximate result of Vendor's gross negligence or willful misconduct; (ii) losses above Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (US $250,000) require independent third-party verification; and (iii) Customer provides written notice and allows Vendor 30 days to investigate and attempt to cure. Documented Clinical Impact Losses shall not include punitive, exemplary or other non-compensatory damages."

Option 3 (Fallback — one-way broader carveout with higher cap):
"Except as provided in this Section, neither Party shall be liable for incidental, consequential, special or punitive damages. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may recover Consequential Damages up to Five Million Dollars (US $5,000,000) where such damages are the direct and proximate result of Vendor's gross negligence, provided that Customer first submits to the dispute resolution procedure in Section Y and presents third-party verification for losses above One Hundred Thousand Dollars (US $100,000)."

My read: Option 2 addresses their business ask while preserving key mitigations (third-party verification, cure window, explicit exclusion of punitive damages). It keeps the exposure bounded and preserves our right to defend and investigate.

If BD wants to push Option 3 for speed, we should accompany it with higher priced commercial terms (one-time implementation fee + slightly higher recurring rate) to offset the incremental risk.

Please confirm which option you want me to send to BrightHealth legal. If yes, I'll prepare a redline with the chosen paragraph and a short cover note framing the mitigations. If no reply by EOD Monday, I'll assume Option 2 and send.

Regards,
